title: CDL driving rules practice questions
description: Free CDL driving rules practice questions on 49 CFR Part 392. Every answer is explained and linked to the section it comes from.

questions.question: What period before going on duty or operating a CMV does 392.5(a)(1) set during which a driver must not use alcohol or be under its influence?

options.A: 4 hours
options.B: 1 hour
options.C: 2 hours
options.D: 30 minutes

questions.explanation: 392.5(a)(1) bars a driver from using alcohol or being under its influence "within 4 hours before going on duty or operating, or having physical control of, a commercial motor vehicle."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 392.5, Alcohol prohibition (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: While a driver is on duty or operating a CMV, what alcohol level does 392.5(a)(2) prohibit?

options.A: An alcohol concentration of 0.04 or greater only
options.B: An alcohol concentration of 0.08 or greater only
options.C: Any measured alcohol concentration or detected presence of alcohol
options.D: Only a level above the State's legal limit for car drivers

questions.explanation: 392.5(a)(2) sets no threshold: a driver must not "have any measured alcohol concentration or detected presence of alcohol, while on duty, or operating, or in physical control of a commercial motor vehicle."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 392.5, Alcohol prohibition (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What out-of-service period does 392.5(c) set for a driver found violating the alcohol prohibition?

options.A: 8 hours
options.B: 24 hours
options.C: 10 hours
options.D: 72 hours

questions.explanation: The driver "shall be placed out-of-service immediately for a period of 24 hours," and the period starts "upon issuance of an out-of-service order."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 392.5, Alcohol prohibition (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Ill or fatigued operator and drugs
questions.question: Under 392.3, when may a driver whose alertness is so impaired by fatigue that driving is unsafe continue to operate a CMV?

options.A: When fewer than 2 hours of driving time remain in the day
options.B: When the dispatcher approves it by phone
options.C: When the load is due at a scheduled appointment
options.D: In a grave emergency where obeying the rule would increase the hazard, only to the nearest place at which that hazard is removed

questions.explanation: Only "in a case of grave emergency where the hazard to occupants of the commercial motor vehicle or other users of the highway would be increased by compliance with this section" may the driver continue "to the nearest place at which that hazard is removed."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 392.3, Ill or fatigued operator (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Ill or fatigued operator and drugs
questions.question: The licensed medical practitioner exception in 392.4(c) covers paragraphs (a)(2), (3) and (4). Which substance category in 392.4(a) does it leave out?

options.A: Amphetamines and their formulations
options.B: Schedule I substances (21 CFR 1308.11)
options.C: Narcotic drugs and their derivatives
options.D: Other substances that could make the driver incapable of safe driving

questions.explanation: 392.4(c) says "Paragraphs (a) (2), (3), and (4) do not apply" to a substance given under a licensed medical practitioner's instructions; paragraph (a)(1), "Any 21 CFR 1308.11 Schedule I substance," is not in that list.

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 392.4, Drugs and other substances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What stopping distance does 392.10(a) set for a CMV that must stop before crossing railroad tracks at grade?

options.A: Within 50 feet of, and not closer than 15 feet to, the tracks
options.B: Within 100 feet of, and not closer than 60 feet to, the tracks
options.C: Within 10 feet of, and not closer than 5 feet to, the tracks
options.D: Within 200 feet of, and not closer than 75 feet to, the tracks

questions.explanation: The driver must first stop "within 50 feet of, and not closer than 15 feet to, the tracks," then listen and look in each direction and make sure no train is approaching.

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 392.10, Railroad grade crossings; stopping required (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Which of these vehicles does 392.10(a) list among the CMVs that must stop before crossing railroad tracks at grade?

options.A: Every truck with more than two axles
options.B: Every vehicle hauling a trailer
options.C: Every property-carrying CMV on an interstate trip
options.D: Every cargo tank motor vehicle, loaded or empty, used to transport any hazardous material

questions.explanation: 392.10(a)(4) lists "Every cargo tank motor vehicle, whether loaded or empty, used for the transportation of any hazardous material." Axle count, trailers and interstate trips are not on the list.

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 392.10, Railroad grade crossings; stopping required (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 392.2, which rule must be complied with when an FMCSA regulation imposes a higher standard of care than the local law of the jurisdiction?

options.A: The local law, because it is where the vehicle is operating
options.B: Whichever rule is less strict
options.C: The FMCSA regulation
options.D: Whichever rule the motor carrier chooses

questions.explanation: A CMV is operated under local law, but "if a regulation of the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration imposes a higher standard of care than that law, ordinance or regulation, the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration regulation must be complied with."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 392.2, Applicable operating rules (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 392.10(b), in which situation need a stop not be made at a railroad grade crossing?

options.A: When a police officer or crossing flagman directs traffic to proceed
options.B: When the driver can see no train within a half mile
options.C: When the crossing is marked only with crossbucks
options.D: When the driver is running behind schedule

questions.explanation: 392.10(b)(2) says a stop need not be made at "A railroad grade crossing when a police officer or crossing flagman directs traffic to proceed."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 392.10, Railroad grade crossings; stopping required (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What does 392.11 require of a CMV not listed in 392.10 as it approaches a railroad grade crossing?

options.A: It may cross at the posted speed limit without slowing
options.B: It must be driven at a speed that lets it stop before the nearest rail, and not cross until due caution shows the course is clear
options.C: It must stop only between sunset and sunrise
options.D: It must sound its horn and may then continue at speed

questions.explanation: Such a CMV must "be driven at a rate of speed which will permit said commercial motor vehicle to be stopped before reaching the nearest rail" and must not cross "until due caution has been taken to ascertain that the course is clear."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 392.11, Railroad grade crossings; slowing down required (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What outer time limit does the general rule in 392.22(b)(1) set for placing warning devices around a CMV stopped on the traveled portion or shoulder of a highway?

options.A: Within 30 minutes
options.B: Within 20 minutes
options.C: Within 1 hour
options.D: As soon as possible, but in any event within 10 minutes

questions.explanation: The driver must place the devices "as soon as possible, but in any event within 10 minutes."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 392.22, Emergency signals; stopped commercial motor vehicles (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 392.22(b)(1)(i), how far from the stopped CMV is the warning device on the traffic side placed, in the direction of approaching traffic?

options.A: 20 paces (approximately 15 meters or 50 feet)
options.B: 1 pace (approximately 1 meter or 3 feet)
options.C: 4 paces (approximately 3 meters or 10 feet)
options.D: 60 paces (approximately 45 meters or 150 feet)

questions.explanation: One device goes "on the traffic side of and 4 paces (approximately 3 meters or 10 feet) from the stopped commercial motor vehicle in the direction of approaching traffic."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 392.22, Emergency signals; stopped commercial motor vehicles (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: For a CMV stopped on a divided or one-way highway, at what distances toward approaching traffic does 392.22(b)(2)(v) place two of the warning devices?

options.A: 50 feet and 25 feet
options.B: 500 feet and 250 feet
options.C: 200 feet and 100 feet
options.D: 300 feet and 150 feet

questions.explanation: The driver places "one warning device at a distance of 200 feet and one warning device at a distance of 100 feet in a direction toward approaching traffic," plus one at the traffic side "within 10 feet of the rear."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 392.22, Emergency signals; stopped commercial motor vehicles (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A CMV is stopped within 500 feet of the crest of a hill. What distance range does 392.22(b)(2)(iv) set for placing the warning signal in the direction of the hill?

options.A: 100 feet to 500 feet from the CMV
options.B: 10 feet to 50 feet from the CMV
options.C: 600 feet to 1,000 feet from the CMV
options.D: 50 feet to 90 feet from the CMV

questions.explanation: The driver places the signal "in the direction of the obstruction to view a distance of 100 feet to 500 feet from the stopped commercial motor vehicle."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 392.22, Emergency signals; stopped commercial motor vehicles (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: For which of these vehicles does 392.25 forbid flame-producing emergency signals?

options.A: Any CMV stopped during daylight hours
options.B: A bus transporting passengers
options.C: A CMV transporting Division 1.4 explosives
options.D: A CMV using compressed gas as a motor fuel

questions.explanation: 392.25 bars flame-producing signals for "any commercial motor vehicle using compressed gas as a motor fuel"; for explosives it names only "Division 1.1, Division 1.2, or Division 1.3."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 392.25, Flame producing devices (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Seat belts, fueling and other practices
questions.question: Under 392.16(b), in which vehicle must all other occupants be properly restrained by seat belts before the driver operates it?

options.A: Only a vehicle hauling hazardous materials
options.B: A property-carrying CMV that has seat belt assemblies installed at the seats for other occupants
options.C: Only a vehicle traveling on an interstate highway
options.D: Only a vehicle whose occupants are motor carrier employees

questions.explanation: 392.16(b) applies to "a property-carrying commercial motor vehicle" that "has seat belt assemblies installed at the seats for other occupants of the vehicle" and requires that "all other occupants are properly restrained."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 392.16, Use of seat belts (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Seat belts, fueling and other practices
questions.question: What does 392.50(c) require of the fuel hose nozzle while a CMV is being fueled?

options.A: It must be held about an inch above the intake pipe
options.B: It must touch the intake pipe only when fueling starts
options.C: It must be watched by a second person
options.D: It must be continuously in contact with the intake pipe of the fuel tank

questions.explanation: No one may fuel a CMV "unless the nozzle of the fuel hose is continuously in contact with the intake pipe of the fuel tank."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 392.50, Ignition of fuel; prevention (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What exception does 392.80(d) allow to the ban on texting while driving a CMV?

options.A: When necessary to communicate with law enforcement officials or other emergency services
options.B: When stopped at a red light with the motor running
options.C: When replying to a message from the dispatcher
options.D: When traveling below 15 miles per hour

questions.explanation: "Texting while driving is permissible by drivers of a commercial motor vehicle when necessary to communicate with law enforcement officials or other emergency services." A stop at a traffic control device with the motor running still counts as driving.

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 392.80, Prohibition against texting (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under the definition in 392.82(b), which of these counts as driving for the hand-held mobile telephone rule?

options.A: Halted at the side of the highway in a location where the vehicle can safely remain stationary
options.B: Halted off the highway at a rest area where the vehicle can safely remain stationary
options.C: Operating a CMV on a highway while temporarily stationary because of traffic
options.D: Halted off the highway at a fuel island where the vehicle can safely remain stationary

questions.explanation: Driving means "operating a commercial motor vehicle on a highway, including while temporarily stationary because of traffic," but not after the driver "has moved the vehicle to the side of, or off, a highway and has halted in a location where the vehicle can safely remain stationary."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 392.82, Using a hand-held mobile telephone (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What distance does 392.9(b)(2) set for the first inspection of cargo and securement devices by a truck or truck tractor driver after beginning a trip?

options.A: Within the first 150 miles
options.B: Within the first 50 miles
options.C: Within the first 100 miles
options.D: Within the first 250 miles

questions.explanation: The driver must "Inspect the cargo and the devices used to secure the cargo within the first 50 miles after beginning a trip" and make any needed adjustments.

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 392.9, Inspection of cargo, cargo securement devices and systems (as of Nov 3, 2026)
